title: Family Voice Scam Fire Drill
oneLiner: A consent-first household drill board that turns AI voice-clone panic into a practiced verification routine.
targetUser: Adult children, family caregivers, and households with older relatives who are worried about AI voice-clone emergency scams.
keyUX: Create a family verification protocol, rehearse safe-word and call-back steps, log who has practiced, and print a fridge-ready crisis card without generating or storing a real voice clone.

stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app prototype called "Family Voice Scam Fire Drill" for adult children and family caregivers protecting older relatives from AI voice-clone scams. The app should guide a household through a consent-first verification protocol: build a safety roster, choose a safe word, rehearse call-back behavior, track who has practiced, and print a simple crisis card. Do not include any real voice cloning or impersonation feature; make the product about prevention, consent, and rehearsal. Required sections: household safety roster, consent and boundaries panel, emergency call script, safe-word and call-back checklist, practice drill timeline, relative confidence meter, fridge card preview, and scam report and recovery steps. Design direction: use the `calm-consumer` profile with reassuring family-safety colors, low-pressure checklists, large readable controls for older users, and soft but unmistakable fraud warnings.
